**ACCEPT** — `domain:cli` execution seat (#6024), 2026-09-12T07:45Z, against head `034629082d7c2b8ae9e50ebb1d6d58035107266e`. Readings below are mine, taken on this head.

### Gate state

`GET /commits/034629082d/check-runs` — **38 checks: 30 `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 red, 1 still running** (`Lint & Repo Gates`). ⭐ All six `Test Core` shards have **completed green** — which is the gate that judges a test-file change, so the substantive measurement is in.

### ⭐ The dev corrected the card's stated mechanism, and it was the mechanism this seat relayed into the dispatch

The card said, and triage repeated, and **this seat's dispatch order repeated again**, that the tenancy provider was invisible *because it is lazy*. The report says that is false. That is the one claim here worth re-measuring independently, because it is the claim this seat passed along without checking:

```
packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts:329   tenancyServiceProvider = async (_environmentId?: string) … {
                                             const kernel = typeof ctx.getKernel === 'function' ? ctx.getKernel() : undefined;
                                             if (kernel && typeof kernel.getServiceAsync === 'function') { try {
packages/rest/src/rest-api-plugin.ts:389   objectQLProvider       = async (_environmentId?: string) … {
                                             const kernel = typeof ctx.getKernel === 'function' ? ctx.getKernel() : undefined;
                                             if (kernel && typeof kernel.getServiceAsync === 'function') { try {
```

The two openings are structurally identical, and `objectQLProvider` at index 7 has **always** been in `PROVIDERS`. ⇒ **laziness was never why the tenancy provider was invisible.** It was invisible because it was **absent from the table**: nothing drove it, so the slot was never asked for, so the set the last case compares could not contain it, so the guard read green against *any* binding at that position.

⭐ The distinction is not rhetorical. On the laziness story the fix might have had to change the comparison — which is exactly the second hard stop this seat wrote into the dispatch. On the real mechanism it is one row. The dev did not accept the relayed mechanism; it measured, and both stops stayed shut for a reason rather than by luck.

### The figures were REMOVED, not corrected — which is what the ruling asked for first

| reading on this head | result |
|:--|:--|
| `sixteen` | **0** |
| `twenty-argument` | **0** |
| `6..19` | **0** |
| control on the same matcher (`provider`) | **25** ⇒ it fires, so the zeros are readings |

The header now says outright that neither figure is written as a numeral **on purpose**, and it distinguishes the two failure modes: the span figures *were accurate the day B4 wrote them and went stale by one*; the slot count *matched no quantity derivable from the file even then*. ⭐ 「先删容许出错的构造,再让正确形态成唯一拼写」 — the erroneous construction here was a hand-typed constant in prose, and it is gone rather than re-typed correctly. The only spelling of either quantity is now one the suite can fail on.

### The new pin, and why it is not a phantom

`NON_PROVIDERS_IN_SPAN` gives the two in-span arguments that are deliberately not providers (index 16, a `(name: string) => boolean` presence probe; index 18, a resolver instance) an explicit home with a stated reason. The new case then derives the span **from the captured constructor call** — `for (let i = firstProvider; i < args.length; i++)` — so an argument appended to `RestServer` falls inside the span **by construction** and must be classified. And it carries the reverse assertion too: no row may point past the end of the argument list, so a removed parameter takes its row with it instead of leaving one that silently asserts nothing.

⇒ the move #15256 made *because* inserting mid-list "would silently re-bind every positional argument after it" now forces a decision in this file instead of landing uncovered.

### The ablation — three legs, and leg A is the card's defect measured directly

- **Leg A, on the PRE-FIX tree**: mis-bind `authServiceProvider` at the last constructor position ⇒ `Tests 5 passed (5)`, **exit 0**. ⭐ The guard stays green against a deliberately mis-bound positional. That is not a control for the fix — **it is the card's defect, reproduced.**
- **Leg B, same mutated blob on the POST-FIX tree** ⇒ exit 1, two failures, the second being `expected Set{…(17)} to deeply equal Set{…(18)}` — **the proof acceptance 1 demanded** that the provider actually enters the compared set, rather than being listed beside it.
- **Leg C**, ablate the new row back out ⇒ exactly **one** red, and it is the new case naming index 20; the other five stay green. A red in isolation, ⛔ not a blanket one.

Each leg proved on disk (grep counts of removed and injected text, `git hash-object` against the HEAD blob) and restored by **state** — blob equality plus an empty `git diff HEAD` — ⛔ not by an exit code. And the absence of a rebuild is stated rather than skipped: the subject is imported as a relative source specifier, so no `dist/` sits between the mutation and the test.

### The `sixteen` derivation, reported per acceptance 4 — and the answer is the interesting one

It was **not** already right, and it was **not** drift. Derived with the TypeScript compiler API — ⛔ explicitly not the bracket-depth counter triage recorded as broken on its own attempt — `rest-api-plugin.ts` resolves **20** distinct slots today. Re-running the same derivation at `1216dcc73`, the single commit that wrote both figures: the span figures were **correct that day**, while the slot count matched **no** quantity derivable from the file even then. ⇒ it was a number with no derivation behind it **from its first commit**, and — the line worth keeping — that is indistinguishable to a reader from one that has since drifted. This card exists because nobody could tell those two apart.

⚠️ Also recorded so nobody repeats the instrument: a runtime `RestServer.length` pin is **not** available. Parameter index 2 carries a default, and `Function.prototype.length` counts only up to the first defaulted parameter, so it reports **2**, not 21.

### Scope and fences

One file. `rest-api-plugin.ts` (landing file of the `pm:on-hold` **#14251**) and `rest-server.ts` are **not in the diff** — the legs A/B mutation was temporary and restored byte-identical. #17672's declared in-flight surface is disjoint, confirmed rather than assumed. The 7 deletions are **entirely docblock prose**; no assertion was weakened and nothing the pin claims was changed. `skip-changeset` applied additively and read back present.

⚠️ One bounded residual the report declares rather than hides: the new span is derived from what the composition root **passes**, so a parameter appended to `RestServer` that the root never passes leaves `args.length` unchanged and the pin green. That is a different defect (a parameter wired nowhere), the case's declared scope says exactly what it covers instead of overclaiming, and closing it would mean parsing `rest-server.ts` from inside a unit test. ⛔ Correctly not filed and ⛔ not widened into here.
